scenario: 2025 IEPR forecast. Mechanism: rate = revenue requirement / sales; 'annual growth in sales (~2.5%/yr 2025-40) offsets continued growth in revenue requirements', so real rates stay roughly flat (slightly declining from the 2024 wildfire-capex peak).
note: EXACT CEC table (was eyeballed from Figure 8; now the machine-readable workbook tn=260210). Values are cents/kWh. Real 2023$ is ~flat ~35c after a 2026 step-down (39->35), nominal rises 40.8->55.1c by 2045. NOTE the base-year definition differs from WhyWatt's: CEC is the blended residential-average rate (~40.8c/kWh nominal 2025) while our model anchors to the E-1 schedule ($0.386/kWh) - a ~6% level difference, not a growth difference. Electricity is real-flat; it does not death-spiral (contrast gas).
